segments.he: אֲבָל נוֹתָר וְהַזְּמַן וְהַטָּמֵא – שָׁוִין בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה.
segments.en: § Following the detailing of the differences between a communal altar and a private altar, the mishna teaches: «But» the halakha that portions of the offering «left over [notar]» beyond the time it is permitted must be burned and that one who eats them incurs karet, «and the» halakha that intent to sacrifice or partake of the offering beyond its designated «time» renders the offering piggul, «and the» prohibition against performing the sacrificial service or eating consecrated meat while «ritually impure are equal in this,» i.e., a private altar, «and that,» i.e., a public altar.

moves.summary: quotes the mishna's list of rules shared by both altars
moves.about: notar, time and impurity apply equally at great and small altars
